title: Can You Eat Before a Root Canal?
metaTitle: Can You Eat Before a Root Canal? What to Know
metaDescription: Should you eat before a root canal? Usually yes, since the tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic. Here is why a meal beforehand helps, and the exceptions.
secondaryKeywords: can you eat before a root canal
excerpt: Unlike surgery under general anaesthetic, a root canal usually lets you eat beforehand. Here is why a meal often helps, and the one exception to keep in mind.
heroImageAlt: A simple, healthy meal on a table before a daytime appointment.
bodyHtml:
Can you eat before a root canal?

In most cases, yes — you can and often should eat a normal meal before a root canal. Unlike surgery performed under general anaesthetic, a standard root canal is done with local anaesthetic (freezing) that numbs only the area around the tooth, so there is usually no need to arrive on an empty stomach. In fact, eating beforehand is often the more comfortable choice, because your mouth will be numb for a few hours afterward and you will want to wait for feeling to return before your next meal. The main exception is if any form of sedation is planned, in which case your clinic will give you specific instructions to follow instead.

Why a meal beforehand usually helps

There are a few practical reasons eating first tends to work in your favour:

  • You will be numb afterward. Local anaesthetic can leave your lip, cheek, and tongue numb for a few hours. Eating during that window risks accidentally biting the inside of your mouth, so most people prefer to have eaten beforehand and wait until sensation returns.
  • Comfort during a longer appointment. Root canals, especially on molars, can take a while. Going in without being hungry helps you feel steadier and more relaxed in the chair.
  • Blood sugar and nerves. Being hungry can make some people feel light-headed or more anxious. A reasonable meal beforehand helps avoid that.

What to eat before your appointment

There are no strict rules, but a balanced, satisfying meal is a good idea — something that keeps you comfortable without leaving food stuck in the tooth that is about to be treated. Brushing afterward so you arrive with a clean mouth is appreciated. If the tooth in question is already sore, simply chew on the other side.

The sedation exception

If you and your dentist have arranged any form of sedation for the appointment, the usual advice changes. Some sedation approaches require you to avoid food or drink for a set period beforehand for safety reasons. This is exactly why it is important to confirm the plan with your clinic ahead of time and follow their specific instructions to the letter. When in doubt, ask.

Should I avoid anything in particular?

You do not need a special diet, but it is sensible to go easy on anything that might aggravate a sensitive tooth right before treatment — for example very hot, very cold, or very sugary items if the tooth is already reacting to those. Otherwise, eat as you normally would.

Does it matter how long before the appointment I eat?

There is no strict timing for a standard root canal with local anaesthetic, but eating within a couple of hours beforehand means you are comfortably full without feeling overly full in the chair. If your appointment is first thing in the morning, a normal breakfast is perfectly reasonable. The goal is simply to avoid being hungry during a potentially longer visit and to have eaten before your mouth goes numb.

Can I drink coffee before a root canal?

Generally yes, though if caffeine tends to make you jittery you might keep it light so you feel calmer in the chair. Staying hydrated with water beforehand is fine and can be more comfortable than arriving thirsty.

What about after the appointment?

Wait until the numbness has fully worn off before eating, to avoid biting your cheek or tongue. When you do eat, soft foods and chewing away from the treated tooth are usually the most comfortable choices for the first little while, and your dentist will give you aftercare guidance specific to your treatment.

Still unsure? Just ask

If you are not certain whether to eat before your particular appointment — especially if sedation might be involved — the simplest thing is to check with the clinic when you book. You can reach the team at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham with any questions, and you can read more about what to expect from root canal therapy at the clinic before your visit. Being clear on this one detail in advance means one less thing to think about on the day.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
